key.description: Whether the provider ships default/built-in commands alongside user-defined custom commands.

builtin_commands.mechanism: 6 built-in slash commands documented as individual headings (/newtask, /smol, /newrule, /deep-planning, /explain-changes, /reportbug); hardcoded, not user-modifiable

key.description: Whether hooks can inject messages, system prompts, or conversation context into the agent's active session.

context_injection.mechanism: context injection documented under 'Context Modification' heading

key.description: What kinds of executors hooks support beyond shell commands. May include HTTP endpoints, LLM prompt evaluation, multi-turn agent handlers, or TypeScript extensions.
key.spec_ref: ACIF-HOOK §10.1 (DERIVABLE); handler-type enum ACIF-HOOK Appendix B, §8.2

handler_types.mechanism: hook handler types documented under 'Hook Types' heading

key.description: Where hooks can be configured and the precedence model when multiple scopes define hooks for the same event. Common scopes: global/user, project, workspace, managed/enterprise.

hook_scopes.mechanism: hook scopes documented under 'Hook Locations' heading (project + global)

key.description: Whether hooks communicate with the host via structured JSON on stdin/stdout rather than plain text or exit codes alone.

json_io_protocol.mechanism: JSON I/O protocol documented under 'Input Structure' / 'Output Structure' headings

key.description: Whether the provider offers an in-IDE MCP server discovery and installation experience.

marketplace.mechanism: in-IDE MCP Marketplace introduced under 'Finding MCP Servers' heading (mcp.0)

key.description: Which MCP transport protocols the provider supports. Common transports: stdio (local process), SSE (Server-Sent Events), HTTP/streamable-HTTP (stateless or streaming).

transport_types.mechanism: transport types documented under 'MCP Transport Mechanisms' / 'STDIO Transport' / 'SSE Transport' headings (mcp.1)

always.mechanism: rules without conditionals load for every request (documented under 'Conditional Rules' / 'How It Works')

glob.mechanism: 'paths' Conditional uses glob-based path matching to scope rule activation (documented under 'The paths Conditional' / 'Writing Conditional Rules')

key.description: How rules decide when to load into context. Providers implement varying modes: always-on, conditional/glob-based, model-decision, and manual activation. Tracks which modes the provider supports and how they are configured.
key.spec_ref: ACIF-RULE §9.1 (DERIVABLE); activation-mode vocabulary ACIF-RULE Appendix A, §10

key.description: Whether rules load from multiple directory levels with defined precedence. Enables project-root rules plus subdirectory-scoped overrides.

hierarchical_loading.mechanism: two-tier scope: Project rules (.clinerules/ in workspace) + Global rules (~/.cline/rules/ user-wide) — documented under 'Where Rules Live' / 'Global Rules Directory'

key.description: The required or conventional filename for this skill type. For example, "SKILL.md" for Claude Code skills.
Whether the skill can be installed at global/personal scope (applies across all projects for the current user).
Whether the skill can be installed at project scope (applies to current project only, typically committed to version control).

skills.frontmatter.mechanism: frontmatter format documented under 'Writing Your SKILL.md' heading

skills.toggling.mechanism: per-skill enable/disable documented under 'Toggling Skills' heading
